other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma innā naj\`aluka fī nuḥūrihim wa na\`ūdhu bika min shurūrihim.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, we ask You to restrain them by their necks, and we seek refuge in You from their evil.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 2/89, and Al-Hakim graded it authentic and Ath-Thahabi agreed 2/142.
tags: Upon encountering an enemy or those of authority

other_duas.category_name: Upon encountering an enemy or those of authority
other_duas.title: Upon encountering an enemy or those of authority
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ أَنْتَ عَضُـدي، وَأَنْتَ نَصـيري، بِكَ أَجـولُ وَبِكَ أَصـولُ وَبِكَ أُقـاتِل
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma anta \`aḍudī, wa anta naṣīrī, bika ajūlu, wa bika aṣūlu, wa bika uqātil.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, You are my strength and You are my support. For Your sake, I go forth and for Your sake, I advance and for Your sake, I fight.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 3/42, At-Tirmidhi 5/572. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/183.
tags: Upon encountering an enemy or those of authority

other_duas.category_name: Upon encountering an enemy or those of authority
other_duas.title: Upon encountering an enemy or those of authority
other_duas.arabic: حَسْبُـنا اللهُ وَنِعْـمَ الوَكـيل
other_duas.transliteration: Ḥasbunallāhu wa ni\`mal-wakīl.
other_duas.translation: Allah is sufficient for us and the best of those on whom to depend.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, 5/172.
tags: Upon encountering an enemy or those of authority

other_duas.category_name: For one afraid of the ruler's injustice
other_duas.title: For one afraid of the ruler's injustice
other_duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ ربَّ السَّمَوَاتِ السَّبْعِ، وَرَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، كُنْ لِي جَاراً مِنْ فُلاَنِ بْنِ فُلاَنٍ، وَأَحْزَابِهِ مِنْ خَلاَئِقِكَ، أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيَّ أَحَدٌ مِنْهُمْ أَوْ يَطْغَى، عَزَّ جَارُكَ، وَجَلَّ ثَنَاؤُكَ، وَلاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma Rabbas-samāwātis-sab\`, wa Rabba ‘l-\`Arshi ‘l-\`Aẓīm, kun lī jāran min \[here you mention the person's name\], wa aḥzābihi min khalā'iqik, an yafruṭa \`alayya aḥadun minhum aw yaṭghā, \`azza jāruk, wa jalla thanā'uk, wa lā ilāha illā ant.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, be for me a support against \[such and such a person\] and his helpers from among your creatures, lest any of them abuse me or do me wrong. Mighty is Your patronage, and glorious are Your praises. There is none worthy of worship but You.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, Al-'Adab Al-Mufrad (no. 707). Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Al-'Adab Al-Mufrad (no. 545).
tags: For one afraid of the ruler's injustice

other_duas.category_name: For one afraid of the ruler's injustice
other_duas.title: For one afraid of the ruler's injustice
other_duas.arabic: الله أكبر، الله أعز من خلقه جميعاً ، الله أعز مما أخاف وأحذر ، أعوذ بالله الذي لا إله إلا هو ، الممسك السموات السبع أن يقعن على الأرض إلا بإذنه ، من شر عبدك فلان ، وجنوده وأتباعه وأشياعه ، من الجن والأنس ، اللهم كن لي جاراً من شرهم ، جل ثناؤك وعز جارك ، وتبارك اسمك ، ولا إله غيرك
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu a\`azzu min khalqihi jamī\`a, Allāhu a\`azzu mimmā akhāfu wa aḥdhar, a\`ūdhu billāhi ‘l-ladhī lā ilāha illā hū, almumsikis-samāwātis-sab\`i an yaqa\`na \`ala ‘l-arḍi illā bi idhnih, min sharri \`abdika \[name of the person\], wa junūdihi wa atbā\`ihi wa ashyā\`ih, mina ‘l-jinni wa ‘l-ins, Allāhumma kun lī jāran min sharrihim, jalla thanā'uk, wa \`azza jāruk, wa tabāraka-smuk, wa lā ilāha ghayruk. Allah is the Most Great, Mightier than all His creation. He is Mightier than what I fear and dread. I seek refuge in Allah, Who there is none worthy of worship but Him. He is the One Who holds the seven heavens from falling upon the earth except by His command. \[I seek refuge in You Allah\] from the evil of Your slave \[name of the person\], and his helpers, his followers, and his supporters from among the jinn and mankind.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, be my support against their evil. Glorious are Your praises and mighty is Your patronage. Blessed is Your Name, there is no true God but You. (Recite three times in Arabic.)
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, 5/172.
tags: For one afraid of the ruler's injustice

other_duas.category_name: Against enemies
other_duas.title: Against enemies
other_duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ مُنْزِلَ الْكِتَاب سَرِيعَ الْحِسَاب اهْزِم الأَحْزَاب اللَّهُمَّ اهْزِمْهُمْ وَ زَلْزِلْهُم
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma munzila ‘l-kitāb, sarī\`a ‘l-ḥisāb, ihzimi ‘l-aḥzāb, Allāhumma-hzimhum wa zalzilhum.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Swift to account, defeat the groups (of disbelievers). O Allah, defeat them and shake them.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 3/1362.

other_duas.category_name: When being afraid of a group of people
other_duas.title: When being afraid of a group of people
other_duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِيهِم بمَا شِئْت
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhummak-finīhim bimā shi't.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, suffice (i.e. protect) me against them however You wish.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 4/2300.
tags: When being afraid of a group of people

other_duas.category_name: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith
other_duas.title: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith
other_duas.arabic: يَسْتَعِيذُ بِاللَّهِ
other_duas.transliteration: A\`ūdhu billāh (Say: )
other_duas.translation: I seek refuge in Allah. (Then you should desist from doing what you are in doubt about.)
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 6/336, Muslim 1/120.
tags: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith

other_duas.category_name: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith
other_duas.title: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith
other_duas.arabic: يقول
other_duas.transliteration: Āmantu billāhi wa Rusulih. (Say: ) I believe in
other_duas.translation: Allah and His Messengers.
tags: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith

other_duas.category_name: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith
other_duas.title: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith
other_duas.arabic: يقرأ قوله تعالى
other_duas.transliteration: Huwa ‘l-Awwalu wa ‘l-Ākhir, waẓ-Ẓāhiru wal-Bāṭin, wa huwa bikulli shay'in \`Alīm. (Recite the Ayat) He is the First and the Last, the Most High and the Most Near. And He is the Knower of all things (in Arabic).
other_duas.reference: Al-Hadid 57:3, Abu Dawud 4/329. Al-Albani graded it good in SahihAbu Dawud, 3/962.
tags: For one afflicted with doubt in his faith

other_duas.category_name: Settling a debt
other_duas.title: Settling a debt
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ اكْفِـني بِحَلالِـكَ عَنْ حَـرامِـك، وَأَغْنِـني بِفَضْـلِكَ عَمَّـنْ سِـواك
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhummak-finī biḥalālika \`an ḥarāmik, wa 'aghninī bi faḍlika \`amman siwāk.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, suffice me with what You have allowed instead of what You have forbidden, and make me independent of all others besides You.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi 5/560. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/180.

other_duas.category_name: Settling a debt
other_duas.title: Settling a debt
other_duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَالْبُخْلِ وَالْجُبْنِ، وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma innī a\`ūdhu bika mina ‘l-ḥammi wa ‘l-ḥazan, wa ‘l-\`ajzi wa ‘l-kasal, wa ‘l-bukhli wa ‘l-jubn, wa ḍala\`id-dayni wa ghalabatir-rijāl.
other_duas.translation: O Allah! I seek refuge with You from worry and grief, from incapacity and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from being heavily in debt and from being overpowered by (other) men.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 7/158.

other_duas.category_name: For one whose affairs have become difficult
other_duas.title: For one whose affairs have become difficult
other_duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ لاَ سَهْلَ إِلاَّ مَا جَعَلْتَهُ سَهْلاً، وَأَنْتَ تَجْعَلُ الْحَزْنَ إِذَا شِئْتَ سَهْلاً
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma lā saḥla illā ma ja\`altahu saḥla wa anta taj\`alu ‘l-ḥazna idhā shi'ta saḥla.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, there is no ease other than what You make easy. If You please You ease sorrow.
other_duas.reference: Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (no. 2427), and Ibn As- Sunni (no. 351). Al-Hafidh (Ibn Hajar) said that this Hadith is authentic. It was also declared authentic by 'Abdul-Qadir Al-Arna'ut in his checking of An-Nawawi's Kitabul-Athkarp. 106.
tags: For one whose affairs have become difficult

other_duas.category_name: Upon committing a sin
other_duas.title: Upon committing a sin
other_duas.arabic: مَا مِنْ عَبْدٍ يُذنِبُ ذَنْباً فَيُحْسِنُ الطُّهُورَ، ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فَيُصَلِّي رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ يَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ إِلاَّ غَفَرَ اللَّهُ لَهُ
other_duas.transliteration: There is not any slave of
other_duas.translation: Allah who commits a sin, then he perfects his purification and stands to pray two Rak'ahs of prayer, then seeks Allah's forgiveness, except that Allah will forgive him.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 2/86, At-Tirmidhi 2/257. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Abu Dawud 1/283.

other_duas.category_name: For expelling the devil and his whisperings
other_duas.title: For expelling the devil and his whisperings
other_duas.arabic: الاستعاذة بالله منه
other_duas.transliteration: A\`ūdhu billāhi minash-shayṭānir-rajīm. Seeking refuge with Allah against him (i.e. by saying
other_duas.translation: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast).
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 1/206, At-Tirmidhi. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 1/77, and Surat Al-Mu'minun, 23:98-9.
tags: For expelling the devil and his whisperings

other_duas.category_name: For expelling the devil and his whisperings
other_duas.title: For expelling the devil and his whisperings
other_duas.arabic: الْأَذَانُ
other_duas.translation: \-- The call to prayer - 'Athan.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 1/291, Al-Bukhari 1/151.
tags: For expelling the devil and his whisperings

other_duas.category_name: For expelling the devil and his whisperings
other_duas.title: For expelling the devil and his whisperings
other_duas.arabic: الْأَذْكَارُ وَقِرَاءَةُ الْقُرْآنِ
other_duas.transliteration: \-- Saying words of
other_duas.translation: Allah's remembrance (Thikr) and recitation of the Qur'an.
other_duas.reference: "Do not turn your homes into graveyards, surely the Devil flees from the house in which Surat Al-Baqarah is read," Muslim 1/539. The Devil is also driven out by the invocations for morning and evening, those that are said before sleeping and upon waking up, those for entering and leaving the house, including those for entering and leaving the mosque, and by many other authentic invocations taught to us by the Prophet (ﷺ) such as the reading of 'Ayatul-Kursi, (Al-Baqarah 2:255), and the last two 'Ayat of Surat Al-Baqarah before going to sleep. Whoever says: "There is none worthy of worship but Allah alone, Who has no partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and he is Able to do all things," one hundred times, it will be a protection for him from the Devil throughout the day.'
tags: For expelling the devil and his whisperings

other_duas.category_name: When stricken with a mishap or overtaken by an affair
other_duas.title: When stricken with a mishap or overtaken by an affair
other_duas.arabic: قَدَّرَ اللهُ وَما شـاءَ فَعَـل
other_duas.transliteration: Qaddarallāhu wa mā shā'a fa\`al. It is the Decree of
other_duas.translation: Allah and He does whatever He wills.
other_duas.reference: "The strong believer is better and more dear to Allah than the weak believer, and in each of them there is good. Be vigilant for what is to your benefit and seek the help of Allah and do not falter. But when you are striken by some setback, do not say: 'If only I had done such and such,' rather say: 'It is the Decree of Allah and He does whatever He wills.' For verily the saying 'if (i.e. if only I had) begins the work of the Devil." Muslim 4/2052.
tags: When stricken with a mishap or overtaken by an affair

other_duas.category_name: Congratulation on the occasion of a birth and its reply
other_duas.title: Congratulation on the occasion of a birth and its reply
other_duas.arabic: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ فِي الْمَوْهُوبِ لَكَ، وَشَكَرْتَ الْوَاهِبَ، وَبَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُ، وَرُزِقْتَ بِرَّهُ
other_duas.transliteration: Bārakallāhu laka fi ‘l-mawhūbi lak, wa shakarta ‘l-wāhib, wa balagha ashuddah, wa ruziqta birrah. The reply of the person being congratulated is to say: Bārakallahu laka wa bāraka \`alayk, wa jazākallāhu khayra, wa razaqakallāhu mithlah, wa ajzala thawābak.
other_duas.translation: May Allah bless you with His gift to you, and may you (the new parent) give thanks, may the child reach the maturity of years, and may you be granted its righteousness. The reply of the person being congratulated is to say: May Allah bless you, and shower His blessings upon you, and may Allah reward you well and bestow upon you its like and reward you abundantly
other_duas.reference: An-Nawawi, Kitdbul-'Athkarp. 349, and Sahihul-'Athkar2/7l3 by Saleem Al-Hilali. (
tags: Congratulation on the occasion of a birth and its reply

other_duas.category_name: Placing childen under Allah’s protection
other_duas.title: Placing childen under Allah’s protection
other_duas.arabic: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعوذ الحسن والحسين
other_duas.transliteration: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to seek Allah's protection for Al-Hasan and Al-Husain by saying: U\`īthukumā bikalimāti ‘llāhit-tāmmati min kulli shayṭānin wa hāmmah, wa min kulli \`aynin lāmmah
other_duas.translation: I seek protection for you in the Perfect Words of Allah from every devil and every beast, and from every envious blameworthy eye.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari4/119.

other_duas.category_name: When visiting the sick
other_duas.title: When visiting the sick
other_duas.arabic: لا بأْسَ طَهـورٌ إِنْ شـاءَ الله
other_duas.transliteration: Lā ba'sa ṭahūrun in shā Allāh. Do not worry, it will be a purification (for you),
other_duas.translation: Allah willing.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani Fathul-Bari 10/118.

other_duas.category_name: When visiting the sick
other_duas.title: When visiting the sick
other_duas.arabic: أَسْـأَلُ اللهَ العَـظيـم، رَبَّ العَـرْشِ العَـظيـم أَنْ يَشْفـيك
other_duas.transliteration: As'alullāha ‘l-\`Aẓīma Rabba ‘l-\`Arshil-\`Aẓīmi an yashfiyak. I ask Almighty
other_duas.translation: Allah, Lord of the Magnificent Throne, to make you well. (Recite seven times in Arabic .)
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/210 and Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 5/180.

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of visiting the sick
other_duas.title: Excellence of visiting the sick
other_duas.arabic: قَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.translation: When a man goes to visit his sick Muslim brother, he walks along a path of Paradise until he sits, and when he sits he is cloaked in mercy. If he comes in the morning, seventy thousand angels pray for him until evening, and if he comes in the evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him until morning. : ( )

other_duas.category_name: When the sick have renounced all hope of life
other_duas.title: When the sick have renounced all hope of life
other_duas.arabic: أللّهُـمَّ اغْفِـرْ لي وَارْحَمْـني وَأَلْحِقْـني بِالرَّفـيقِ الأّعْلـى
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma’ghfir lī warḥamnī wa alḥiqnī bir-rafīqi ‘l-'A\`alā.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, forgive me and have mercy upon me, and join me with the highest companions (in Paradise).
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari7/10, Muslim 4/1893.
tags: When the sick have renounced all hope of life

other_duas.category_name: When the sick have renounced all hope of life
other_duas.title: When the sick have renounced all hope of life
other_duas.arabic: جعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عند موته يدخل يديه في الماء فيمسح بهما وجههُ ويقول
other_duas.transliteration: As he was dying, the Prophet (ﷺ) dipped his hands in water and wiped his face saying: Lā ilāha illallāh inna li ‘lmawti la’sakarāt.
other_duas.translation: There is none worthy of worship but Allah, surely death has agonies.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 8/144. The Hadith also mention him using the Siivak (tooth stick).
tags: When the sick have renounced all hope of life

other_duas.category_name: When the sick have renounced all hope of life
other_duas.title: When the sick have renounced all hope of life
other_duas.arabic: لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ وَاللّهُ أَكْبَـر، لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ وحْـدَهُ، لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ وحْـدَهُ لا شَريكَ لهُ، لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ لهُ المُلكُ ولهُ الحَمْد، لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ وَلا حَـوْلَ وَلا قُـوَّةَ إِلاّ بِالله
other_duas.transliteration: Lā ilāha illallāh wallāhu Akbar, lā ilāha illallāhu waḥdah, lā ilāha illallāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lā ilāha illallāh lahu ‘l-mulku wa lahu ‘l-ḥamd, lā ilāha illallāh wa lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāh.
other_duas.translation: There is none worthy of worship but Allah, Allah is the Most Great. None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone. None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, Who has no partner. There is none worthy of worship but Allah, His is the dominion and His is the praise. There is none worthy of worship but Allah, there is no power and no might but by Allah.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/152 and Sahih Ibn Majah 2/317.
tags: When the sick have renounced all hope of life

other_duas.category_name: Instruction for the one nearing death
other_duas.title: Instruction for the one nearing death
other_duas.arabic: من كان آخر كلامه
other_duas.transliteration: Lā ilāha illallāh Whoever dies with the last words (whose meaning is): "
other_duas.translation: There is none worthy of worship but Allah" will enter Paradise.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 3/190. See also Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 5/432.
tags: Instruction for the one nearing death

other_duas.category_name: For one afflicted by a calamity
other_duas.title: For one afflicted by a calamity
other_duas.arabic: إِنّا للهِ وَإِنَا إِلَـيْهِ راجِعـون ، اللهُـمِّ اْجُـرْني في مُصـيبَتي، وَاخْلُـفْ لي خَيْـراً مِنْـها
other_duas.transliteration: Innā lillāhi wa innā ilayhi rāji\`ūn, Allāhumma-jurni fī muṣībatī wa 'khluf lī khayran minhā. We are from Allah and unto Him we return.
other_duas.translation: O Allah take me out of my plight and bring to me after it something better.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/632.
tags: For one afflicted by a calamity

other_duas.category_name: When closing the eyes of the deceased
other_duas.title: When closing the eyes of the deceased
other_duas.arabic: اللهُـمِّ اغْفِـرْ لِـفلان
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma’ghfir li (name of the person) warfa\` darajatahu fi ‘l-mahdiyyīn, wakhlufhu fī \`aqibihi fi ‘l-ghābirīn, wagh’fir-lanā wa lahu yā Rabba ‘l-\`ālamīn, wafsaḥ lahu fī qabrihi wa nawwir lahu fīh.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, forgive \[name of the person\] and elevate his station among those who are guided. Send him along the path of those who came before, and forgive us and him, O Lord of the worlds. Enlarge for him his grave, and shed light upon him in it.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/634.
tags: When closing the eyes of the deceased

other_duas.category_name: Condolence
other_duas.title: Condolence
other_duas.arabic: إن لله ما أخذ وله ما أعطى
other_duas.transliteration: Inna lillāhi mā akhadh, wa lahu mā a\`tā, wa kullu shay'in \`indahu bi ajalin musammā . . . faltaṣbir wa ‘l-taḥtasib . \[Also good to say: \] A\`ẓamallāhu ajrak, wa 'aḥsana \`azā'ak, wa ghafara limayyitik. Surely, Allah takes what is His, and what He gives is His, and to all things He has appointed a time... so have patience and be rewarded.1
other_duas.translation: May Allah magnify your reward, and make perfect your bereavement, and forgive your departed.2
other_duas.reference: 1 Al-Bukhari 2/80, Muslim 2/636. 2An-Nawawi, Kitabul-'Athkar, p. 126. "

other_duas.category_name: Placing the deceased in the grave
other_duas.title: Placing the deceased in the grave
other_duas.arabic: بِسْـمِ اللهِ وَعَلـى سُـنَّةِ رَسـولِ الله
other_duas.transliteration: Bismillāh wa \`alā sunnati Rasūlillāh. With the Name of
other_duas.translation: Allah, and according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 3/314 with an authentic chain. Ahmad also recorded it with the wording: With the Name of Allah, and according to the religion of the Messenger of Allah. Its chain is also authentic.
tags: Placing the deceased in the grave

other_duas.category_name: After burying the deceased
other_duas.title: After burying the deceased
other_duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْهُ
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma’ghfir lah Allāhumma thabbit’h.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, strengthen him.
other_duas.reference: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to stop after burying the dead and say to the people: "Ask Allah to forgive your brother and pray for him to be strengthened, for indeed he is now being questioned." Abu Dawud 3/315, and Al-Hakim 1/370 who graded it authentic and Ath-Thahabi agreed.

other_duas.category_name: Visiting the graves
other_duas.title: Visiting the graves
other_duas.arabic: السَّلامُ عَلَـيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيارِ مِنَ المؤْمِنيـنَ وَالْمُسْلِمين، وَإِنّا إِنْ شاءَ اللهُ بِكُـمْ لاحِقـون، نَسْـاَلُ اللهَ لنـا وَلَكُـمْ العـافِيَة
other_duas.transliteration: Assalāmu \`alaykum ahlad-diyāri minal-mu'minīna wa ‘l-muslimīn, wa innā in shā' Allāhu bikum lāḥiqūn nas'alullāha lanā wa lakumul-\`āfiyah. Peace be upon you, people of this abode, from among the believers and those who are Muslims, and we, by the Will of Allah, shall be joining you. \[
other_duas.translation: May Allah have mercy on the first of us and the last of us\] I ask Allah to grant us and you well-being.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/671, Ibn Majah 1/494, the portion brackets is from Muslim 2/671.

other_duas.category_name: During a wind storm
other_duas.title: During a wind storm
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ إِنَّـي أَسْـأَلُـكَ خَيْـرَها، وَأَعـوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَـرِّها
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayrahā, wa a\`ūdhu bika min sharrihā.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, I ask You for the good of it, and seek refuge in You against its evil.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 4/326, Ibn Majah 2/1228. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 2/305.

other_duas.category_name: During a wind storm
other_duas.title: During a wind storm
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ إِنَّـي أَسْـأَلُـكَ خَيْـرَها، وَخَيْـرَ ما فيهـا، وَخَيْـرَ ما اُرْسِلَـتْ بِه، وَأَعـوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَـرِّها، وَشَـرِّ ما فيهـا، وَشَـرِّ ما اُرْسِلَـتْ بِه
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayrahā, wa khayra mā fīhā, wa khayra mā ursilat bih, wa a\`ūdhu bika min sharrihā, wa sharri mā fīhā, wa sharri mā ursilat bih.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, I ask You for the good of it, for the good of what it contains, and for the good of what is sent with it. I seek refuge in You from the evil of it, from the evil of what it contains, and from the evil that is sent with it.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/616, Al-Bukhari 4/76.

other_duas.category_name: Upon hearing thunder
other_duas.title: Upon hearing thunder
other_duas.arabic: سُبْـحانَ الّذي يُسَبِّـحُ الـرَّعْدُ بِحَمْـدِهِ، وَالملائِكـةُ مِنْ خيـفَته
other_duas.transliteration: Subḥāna ‘l-ladhī yusabbiḥur-ra\`du bi ḥamdihi wa ‘l-malā'ikatu min khīfatih.
other_duas.translation: Glory is to Him Whom thunder and angels glorify due to fear of Him.
other_duas.reference: Whenever Abdullah bin Zubair (RA) would hear thunder, he would abandon all conversation and say this supplication. See Al-Muwatta' 2/992. It was graded authentic by Al-Albani as a statement of Abdullah bin Zubayr only.

other_duas.category_name: For rain
other_duas.title: For rain
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُمَّ اسْقِـنا غَيْـثاً مُغيـثاً مَريئاً مُريـعاً، نافِعـاً غَيْـرَ ضار، عاجِـلاً غَـيْرَ آجِل
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma ‘asqinā ghaythan mughīthan marī'an murī\`a, nāfi\`an ghayra ḍārr, \`ājilan ghayra ājil.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, shower upon us abundant rain, beneficial not harmful, swiftly and not delayed.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 1/303. See also Al-Albani SahihAbu Dawud 1/216.

other_duas.category_name: For rain
other_duas.title: For rain
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُمَّ أغِثْنـا، اللّهُمَّ أغِثْنـا، اللّهُمَّ أغِثْنـا
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma aghithnā, Allāhumma aghithnā, Allāhumma aghithnā.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain. O Allah, send us rain.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 1/224, Muslim 2/613.

other_duas.category_name: For rain
other_duas.title: For rain
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُمَّ اسْقِ عِبادَكَ وَبَهـائِمَك، وَانْشُـرْ رَحْمَـتَكَ وَأَحْيِي بَلَـدَكَ المَيِّـت
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma’sqi \`ibādaka wa bahā'imak, wanshur raḥmatak, wa aḥyi baladaka ‘l-mayyit
other_duas.translation: O Allah, give water to Your slaves, and Your livestock, and spread Your mercy, and revive Your dead land.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 1/305. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih Abu Dawud 1/218.

other_duas.category_name: When it rains
other_duas.title: When it rains
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُمَّ صَيِّـباً نافِـعاً
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma ṣayyiban nāfi\`a.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, (bring) beneficial rain clouds.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 2/518.

other_duas.category_name: After rainfall
other_duas.title: After rainfall
other_duas.arabic: مُطِـرْنا بِفَضْـلِ اللهِ وَرَحْمَـتِه
other_duas.transliteration: Muṭirnā bifaḍlillāhi wa raḥmatih. We have been given rain by the grace and mercy of
other_duas.translation: Allah.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 1/205, Muslim 1/83.

other_duas.category_name: Asking for clear skies
other_duas.title: Asking for clear skies
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُمَّ حَوالَيْنا وَلا عَلَيْـنا، اللّهُمَّ عَلى الآكـامِ وَالظِّـراب، وَبُطـونِ الأوْدِية، وَمَنـابِتِ الشَّجـر
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma ḥawālaynā wa lā \`alaynā. Allāhumma \`ala ‘l-ākāmi waẓ-ẓirāb, wa buṭūni ‘l-awdiyati, wa manābitish-shajar.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, let the rain fall around us and not upon us, O Allah, (let it fall) on the pastures, hills, valleys, and the roots of trees.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 1/224, Muslim 1/614

other_duas.category_name: Upon sighting the crescent moon
other_duas.title: Upon sighting the crescent moon
other_duas.arabic: اللهُ أَكْـبَر، اللّهُمَّ أَهِلَّـهُ عَلَيْـنا بِالأمْـنِ وَالإيمـان، والسَّلامَـةِ والإسْلام، وَالتَّـوْفيـقِ لِما تُحِـبُّ رَبَّنـا وَتَـرْضـى، رَبُّنـا وَرَبُّكَ الله
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhu Akbar, Allāhumma ahillahu \`alayna bi ‘l-amni wa ‘l-īmān, was-salāmati wa ‘l-'Islām, wat-tawfīqi limā tuḥibbu Rabbanā wa tarḍā, Rabbunā wa Rabbukallāh. Allah is the Most Great.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, bring us the new moon with security and Faith, with peace and in Islam, and in harmony with what our Lord loves and what pleases Him. Our Lord and your Lord is Allah.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi 5/504, Ad-Darimi 1/336. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/157.

other_duas.category_name: Upon breaking fast
other_duas.title: Upon breaking fast
other_duas.arabic: ذَهَـبَ الظَّمَـأُ، وَابْتَلَّـتِ العُـروق، وَثَبَـتَ الأجْـرُ إِنْ شـاءَ الله
other_duas.transliteration: Dhahabaẓ-ẓama', wabtallati ‘l-\`urūq, wa thabata ‘l-'ajru in shā Allāh. The thirst is gone, the veins are moistened, and the reward is confirmed, if
other_duas.translation: Allah wills.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 2/306 and others. See also Al- Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 4/209.

other_duas.category_name: Upon breaking fast
other_duas.title: Upon breaking fast
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ إِنَّـي أَسْـأَلُـكَ بِرَحْمَـتِكَ الّتي وَسِـعَت كُلَّ شيء، أَنْ تَغْـفِرَ لي
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma innī as'aluka bi raḥmatika ‘l-latī wasi\`at kulla shay' an taghfira lī.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, I ask You by Your mercy, which encompasses all things, that You forgive me.
other_duas.reference: Ibn Majah 1/557 from a supplication of Abdullah bin 'Amr. Al-Hafidh graded it as good in his checking of An-Nawawi's Kitabul-'Athkdr. See Sharhul- Athkar 4/342.

other_duas.category_name: Before eating
other_duas.title: Before eating
other_duas.arabic: إِذَا أَكَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ طَعَاماً فَلْيَقُلْ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ، فَإِنْ نَسِيَ فِي أَوَّلِهِ فَلْيَقُلْ بسمِ اللَّهِ فِي أَوَّلِهِ وَآخِرِهِ
other_duas.transliteration: When anyone of you begins eating, say: Bismillāh. And if you forget then when you remember, say: Bismillāhi fī awwalihi wa ākhirih. When anyone of you begins eating, say: With the Name of
other_duas.translation: Allah. And if you forget then, when you remember, say: With the Name of Allah, in the beginning, and in the end.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 3/347, At-Tirmidhi 4/288. See Al- Albani's Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/167.

other_duas.category_name: Before eating
other_duas.title: Before eating
other_duas.arabic: مَنْ أَطْعَمَهُ اللَّهُ الطَّعَامَ فَلْيَقُلْ
other_duas.transliteration: Whomever Allah has given food, should say: Allāhumma bārik lanā fīhi, wa aṭ\`imnā khayran minh. Whomever Allah has given milk to drink, should say : Allāhumma bārik lanā fīhi, wa zidnā minh. Whomever Allah has given food, should say:
other_duas.translation: O Allah, bless us in it and provide us with better than it. Whomever Allah has given milk to drink, should say : O Allah, bless us in it and give us more of it.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi 5/506. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/158.

other_duas.category_name: Upon completing the meal
other_duas.title: Upon completing the meal
other_duas.arabic: الْحَمْـدُ للهِ الَّذي أَطْعَمَنـي هـذا وَرَزَقَنـيهِ مِنْ غَـيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلا قُوَّة
other_duas.transliteration: Alhamdu lillāhi ‘l-ladhī aṭ\`amanī hādhā, wa razaqanīhi min ghayri ḥawlin minnī wa lā quwwah.
other_duas.translation: Praise is to Allah Who has given me this food, and sustained me with it though I was unable to do it and powerless.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/159.

other_duas.category_name: Upon completing the meal
other_duas.title: Upon completing the meal
other_duas.arabic: الْحَمْـدُ للهِ حَمْـداً كَثـيراً طَيِّـباً مُبـارَكاً فيه، غَيْرَ مَكْفِيٍّ وَلا مُوَدَّعٍ وَلا مُسْتَغْـنىً عَنْـهُ رَبَّـنا
other_duas.transliteration: Alhamdu lillāhi ḥamdan kathīran tayyiban mubārakan fīh, ghayra makfiyyin wa lā muwadda\`in, wa lā mustaghnan \`anhu Rabbanā.
other_duas.translation: All praise is to Allah, praise in abundance, good and blessed. It cannot \[be compensated for, nor can it\] be left, nor can it be done without, our Lord.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 6/214, At-Tirmidhi 5/507.

other_duas.category_name: Of the guest for the host
other_duas.title: Of the guest for the host
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ بارِكْ لَهُمْ فيما رَزَقْـتَهُم، وَاغْفِـرْ لَهُـمْ وَارْحَمْهُمْ
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma bārik lahum fī mā razaqtahum, wagh’fir lahum warḥamhum.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, bless them in what You have provided for them, and forgive them and have mercy on them.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 3/1615.
tags: Of the guest for the host

other_duas.category_name: To one who intends to give food or drink
other_duas.title: To one who intends to give food or drink
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ أَطْعِمْ مَن أَطْعَمَني، وَاسْقِ مَن سقاني
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma aṭ\`im man aṭ\`amanī wasqi man saqānī.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, feed the one who has fed me, and give drink to the one who has given me drink.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 3/126.
tags: To one who intends to give food or drink

other_duas.category_name: By one fasting when presented with food and does not break his fast
other_duas.title: By one fasting when presented with food and does not break his fast
other_duas.arabic: إِذَا دُعِيَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيُجِبْ، فَإِنْ كَانَ صَائِماً فَلْيُصَلِّ، وَإِنْ كَانَ مُفْطِراً فَلْيَطْعَمْ
other_duas.transliteration: \-- When you are invited (to eat) then reply to the invitation. If you are fasting then invoke
other_duas.translation: Allah's blessings (on your host), and if you are not fasting then eat.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/1054. (
tags: By one fasting when presented with food and does not break his fast

other_duas.category_name: When insulted while fasting
other_duas.title: When insulted while fasting
other_duas.arabic: إِنِّي صَائِمٌ، إِنِّي صَائِمٌ
other_duas.transliteration: Innī ṣā'im, innī ṣā'im. I am fasting. I am fasting.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-BAri 4/103, Muslim 2/806.

other_duas.category_name: Upon seeing the early or premature fruit
other_duas.title: Upon seeing the early or premature fruit
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ بارِكْ لَنا في ثَمَـرِنا، وَبارِكْ لَنا في مَدينَتِنـا، وَبارِكْ لَنا في صاعِنـا، وَبارِكْ لَنا في مُدِّنا
other_duas.transliteration: Allahumma bārik lanā fī thamarinā, wa bārik lanā fī madīnatinā wa bārik lanā fī ṣā\`inā, wa bārik lanā fī muddinā.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, bless us in our dates and bless us in our town, bless us in our Sa' and in our Mudd.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/1000 (Sa' and Mudd are both dry measures used for agricultural produce by the Arabs in the Prophet's time. Of the two, the So.' was the larger measure.) (Translator)
tags: Upon seeing the early or premature fruit

other_duas.category_name: Upon sneezing
other_duas.title: Upon sneezing
other_duas.arabic: إِذَا عَطَسَ أَحَدُكُم فَلْيَقُلِ
other_duas.transliteration: When you sneeze , then say : Alḥamdulillāh Your companion should say : Yarḥamukallāh When someone says Yarḥamukallāh to you then you should say: Yahdīkumu ‘llāhu wa yuṣliḥu bālakum. When you sneeze, then say:
other_duas.translation: All praises and thanks are to Allah. Your companion should say: May Allah have mercy upon you. When someone says Yarḥamukallāh to you then you should say: May Allah guide you and set your affairs in order.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 7/125.

other_duas.category_name: When a disbeliever praises Allah after sneezing
other_duas.title: When a disbeliever praises Allah after sneezing
other_duas.arabic: يَهْـديكُـمُ اللهُ وَيُصْـلِحُ بالَـكُم
other_duas.transliteration: Yahdīkumullāhu wa yuṣliḥu bālakum.
other_duas.translation: May Allah guide you and set your affairs in order
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi 5/82, Ahmad 4/400, Abu Dawud 4/ 308. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/354.
tags: When a disbeliever praises Allah after sneezing

other_duas.category_name: To the newlywed
other_duas.title: To the newlywed
other_duas.arabic: بارَكَ اللّهُ لَك، وَبارَكَ عَلَـيْك، وَجَمَعَ بَيْـنَكُما في خَـيْر
other_duas.transliteration: Bārakallāhu lak, wa bāraka \`alayk, wa jama\`a baynakumā fī khayr.
other_duas.translation: May Allah bless you, and shower His blessings upon you, and join you together in goodness.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah and At-Tirmidhi. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 1/316.

other_duas.category_name: On the wedding night or when buying an animal
other_duas.title: On the wedding night or when buying an animal
other_duas.arabic: إِذَا تَزَوَّجَ أَحَدُكُمُ امْرَأَةً، أَوْ إِذَا اشْتَرَى خَادِماً فَلْيَقُلْ
other_duas.transliteration: When any of you marries a woman or purchases a maid-servant then let him say: Allāhumma innī as'aluka khayrahā wa khayra mā jabaltahā \`alayh, wa a\`ūdhu bika min sharrihā wa sharri mā jabaltahā \`alayh. When any of you marries a woman or purchases a maid-servant then let him say :
other_duas.translation: O Allah, I ask You for the goodness of her, and the goodness upon which You have created her, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of her, and from the evil upon which You have created her. If you purchase a camel then take hold of the top of its hump and say the same.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 2/248 and Ibn Majah 1/617. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 1/324.
tags: On the wedding night or when buying an animal

other_duas.category_name: Before sexual intercourse with the wife
other_duas.title: Before sexual intercourse with the wife
other_duas.arabic: بِسْمِ الله اللّهُـمَّ جَنِّبْنا الشَّيْـطانَ، وَجَنِّبِ الشَّـيْطانَ ما رَزَقْـتَنا
other_duas.transliteration: Bismillāh. Allāhumma jannibnash-Shayṭān, wa jannibish-Shayṭāna mā razaqtanā. With the Name of Allah.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, keep the Devil away from us, and keep the Devil away from that which You provide for us.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 6/141, Muslim 2/1028.
tags: Before sexual intercourse with the wife

other_duas.category_name: When angry
other_duas.title: When angry
other_duas.arabic: أَعـوذُ بِاللهِ مِنَ الشَّيْـطانِ الرَّجيـم
other_duas.transliteration: A\`ūdhu billāhi minash-Shayṭānir-rajīm.
other_duas.translation: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 7/99, Muslim 4/2015.

other_duas.category_name: Upon seeing someone in trial or tribulation
other_duas.title: Upon seeing someone in trial or tribulation
other_duas.arabic: الْحَمْـدُ للهِ الّذي عافاني مِمّا ابْتَـلاكَ بِهِ، وَفَضَّلَـني عَلى كَثيـرٍ مِمَّنْ خَلَـقَ تَفْضـيلا
other_duas.transliteration: Alhamdu lillāhi ‘l-ladhī \`āfānī mimmab-talāka bihi wa faḍḍalanī \`alā kathīrin mimman khalaqa tafḍīlā.
other_duas.translation: Praise is to Allah Who has spared me what He has afflicted you with, and preferred me greatly above much of what He has created.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi 5/493,4. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/153.
tags: Upon seeing someone in trial or tribulation

other_duas.category_name: At a sitting or gathering
other_duas.title: At a sitting or gathering
other_duas.arabic: عن ابن عمر قال
other_duas.transliteration: Ibn Umar (ra) said:
other_duas.translation: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to repeat in a single sitting: Rabbigh’fir lī wa tub \`alayy innaka antat-Tawwābu ‘l-Ghafūr. Ibn Umar (ra) said: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) used to repeat in a single sitting: My Lord, forgive me, and accept my repentance, You are the Ever-Relenting, the All-Forgiving.
other_duas.reference: Sahih Ibn Majah 2/321. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/153.

other_duas.category_name: For the expiation of sins, said at the conclusion of a sitting or gathering
other_duas.title: For the expiation of sins, said at the conclusion of a sitting or gathering
other_duas.arabic: سُبْحـانَكَ اللّهُـمَّ وَبِحَمدِك، أَشْهَـدُ أَنْ لا إِلهَ إِلاّ أَنْتَ أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتوبُ إِلَـيْك
other_duas.transliteration: Subhānaka Allāhumma wa biḥamdik, ash-hadu an lā ilāha illā ant, astaghfiruka wa atību ilayk. Glory is to You,
other_duas.translation: O Allah, and praise is to You. I bear witness that there is none worthy of worship but You. I seek Your forgiveness and repent to You.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, At-Tirmidhi and An-Nasa'i. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/ 153. Aishah (RA) said: "Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) did not sit in a gathering, and did not recite the Qur'an, and did not perform any prayer without concluding by saying ... (then she quoted the above)." This was reported by An-Nasa'i in 'Amalul-Yawm wal-Laylah (no.308), and Dr. Farooq Hamadah graded it authentic in his checking of the same book, p. 273. See also Ahmad 6/77
tags: For the expiation of sins, said at the conclusion of a sitting or gathering

other_duas.category_name: To one who does you a favour
other_duas.title: To one who does you a favour
other_duas.arabic: جَزاكَ اللهُ خَـيْراً
other_duas.transliteration: Jazākallāhu khayra.
other_duas.translation: May Allah reward you with good.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi (no. 2035). See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/200 and Sahihul-Jami' (no. 6244).
tags: To one who does you a favour

other_duas.category_name: Protection from the Dajjal
other_duas.title: Protection from the Dajjal
other_duas.arabic: مَنْ حَفِظَ عَشْرَ آيَاتٍ مِنْ أَوَّلِ سُورَةِ الْكَهْفِ عُصِمَ مِنَ الدَّجَّالِ
other_duas.transliteration: \-- Whoever memorizes ten 'Ayat (Verses) from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf, will be protected from the False Messiah 1 if he recites in every prayer after the final Tashahhud before ending the prayer, seeking the protection of
other_duas.translation: Allah from the trials of the False Messiah.
other_duas.reference: 1 Muslim 1/555, another version mentions the last ten 'Ayat, Muslim 1/556. 2 See invocations no. 55 and 56 of this book. .(

other_duas.category_name: To one who pronounces his love for you, for Allah’s sake
other_duas.title: To one who pronounces his love for you, for Allah’s sake
other_duas.arabic: أَحَبَّـكَ الّذي أَحْبَبْـتَني لَه
other_duas.transliteration: Aḥabbaka ‘lladhī aḥbabtanī lah. May He for Whose sake you love me, love you.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 4/333. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih Abu Dawud 3/965.
tags: To one who pronounces his love for you, for Allah’s sake

other_duas.category_name: To one who has offered you some of his wealth
other_duas.title: To one who has offered you some of his wealth
other_duas.arabic: بارَكَ اللهُ لَكَ في أَهْلِكَ وَمالِك
other_duas.transliteration: Bārakallāhu laka fī ahlika wa mālik.
other_duas.translation: May Allah bless you in your family and your property.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-BAri 4/88.
tags: To one who has offered you some of his wealth

other_duas.category_name: To the debtor when his debt is settled
other_duas.title: To the debtor when his debt is settled
other_duas.arabic: بارَكَ اللهُ لَكَ في أَهْلِكَ وَمالِك، إِنَّما جَـزاءُ السَّلَفِ الْحَمْدُ والأَداء
other_duas.transliteration: Bārakallāhu laka fī ahlika wa mālik, innamā jazā'us-salafi ‘l-ḥamdu wa‘l-adā'.
other_duas.translation: May Allah bless you in your family and your wealth, surely the reward for a loan is praise and returning (what was borrowed).
other_duas.reference: An-Nasa'i, 'Amalul-Yawm wal-Laylahp. 300, Ibn Majah 2/809. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah2/55.
tags: To the debtor when his debt is settled

other_duas.category_name: To someone who says "May Allah bless you"
other_duas.title: To someone who says "May Allah bless you"
other_duas.arabic: وَفيكَ بارَكَ الله
other_duas.transliteration: Wafīka bārakallāh. And may
other_duas.translation: Allah bless you.
other_duas.reference: Ibn As-Sunni, p. 138, (no. 278). See also Ibn Al-Qayyim, Al-Wdbil As-Sayyib, p. 304, with checking by Basheer Muhammad ?Uyoon.
tags: To someone who says "May Allah bless you"

other_duas.category_name: The scorn of ascribing things to evil omens
other_duas.title: The scorn of ascribing things to evil omens
other_duas.arabic: اللّهُـمَّ لا طَيْـرَ إِلاّ طَيْـرُك، وَلا خَـيْرَ إِلاّ خَـيْرُك، وَلا إِلهَ غَيْـرُك
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma lā ṭayra illā ṭayruk, wa lā khayra illā khayruk, wa lā ilāha ghayruk.
other_duas.translation: O Allah there is no portent other than Your portent, no goodness other than Your goodness, and none worthy of worship other than You.
other_duas.reference: Ahmad 2/220, Ibn As-Sunni (no. 292). See also Al-Albani, Silsilatul-'Ahadlth As-Sahihah 3/54, (no. 1065). As for bodings of good, these used to please the Prophet (ﷺ) and so when he heard good words from someone, he used to say: "We have taken from you a good portent from your mouth," Abu Dawud, Ahmad. See also Al-Albani, Silsilatul-'Ahadith As-Sahihah 2/363, and it is with Abu Ash-Shaikh Al-Asfahani in 'Akhlaqun-Nabiyy, pg. 270.
tags: The scorn of ascribing things to evil omens

other_duas.category_name: When mounting an animal or any means of transport
other_duas.title: When mounting an animal or any means of transport
other_duas.arabic: بِسْـمِ اللهِ وَالْحَمْـدُ لله،
other_duas.transliteration: Bismillāh, walḥamdulillāh. Subḥāna ‘lladhī sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn. Wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn. Alḥamdulillāh, alḥamdulillāh, alḥamdulillāh, Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Subḥānaka ‘llāhumma innī ẓalamtu nafsī, faghfir lī, fa innahu lā yaghfirudh-dhunūba illā ant. With the Name of Allah. Praise is to Allah. Glory is to Him Who has provided this for us though we could never have had it by our efforts. Surely, unto our Lord, we are returning. Praise is to Allah. Praise is to Allah. Praise is to Allah. Allah is the Most Great. Allah is the Most Great. Allah is the Most Great. Glory is to You.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, I have wronged my own soul. Forgive me, for surely none forgives sins but You.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 3/34, At-Tirmidhi 5/501. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi3/156.
tags: When mounting an animal or any means of transport

other_duas.category_name: For travel
other_duas.title: For travel
other_duas.arabic: اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ،
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Allāhu Akbar, Subḥāna ‘l-ladhi sakhkhara lanā hādhā wa mā kunnā lahu muqrinīn. Wa innā ilā Rabbinā lamunqalibūn. Allāhumma innā nas'aluka fī safarinā hādha ‘l-birra wat-taqwā, Wa mina ‘l-\`amali mā tarḍā, Allāhumma hawwin \`alaynā safaranā hādhā waṭwi \`annā bu\`dah, Allāhumma antas-sāḥibu fis-safar, wa ‘l-khalīfatu fil-ahl, Allāhumma innī a\`ūdhu bika min wa\`thā'is-safar, wa ka'ābati ‘l-manẓar, wa sū'il-munqalabi fil-māli wa ‘l-ahl. (Upon returning recite the same again adding): Ā’ibūna, tā'ibūna, \`ābidūn, Li Rabbinā ḥāmidūn. Allah is the Most Great. Allah is the Most Great. Allah is the Most Great. Glory is to Him Who has provided this for us though we could never have had it by our efforts. Surely, unto our Lord we are returning.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, we ask You on this our journey for goodness and piety, and for works that are pleasing to You. O Allah, lighten this journey for us and make its distance easy for us. O Allah, You are our Companion on the road and the One in Whose care we leave our family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from this journey's hardships, and from the wicked sights in store and from finding our family and property in misfortune upon returning. (Upon returning recite the same again adding :) We return repentant to our Lord, worshipping our Lord, and praising our Lord.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/978. "

other_duas.category_name: Upon entering a town or village
other_duas.title: Upon entering a town or village
other_duas.arabic: أللّـهُمَّ رَبَّ السَّـمواتِ السّـبْعِ وَما أَظْلَلَـن، وَرَبَّ الأَراضيـنَ السّـبْعِ وَما أقْلَلْـن، وَرَبَّ الشَّيـاطينِ وَما أَضْلَلْـن، وَرَبَّ الرِّياحِ وَما ذَرَيْـن، أَسْـأَلُـكَ خَيْـرَ هذهِ الْقَـرْيَةِ وَخَيْـرَ أَهْلِـها، وَخَيْـرَ ما فيها، وَأَعـوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَـرِّها وَشَـرِّ أَهْلِـها، وَشَـرِّ ما فيها
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma Rabbas-samāwātis-sab\`i wa mā aẓlaln, Wa Rabba ‘l-arāḍīnas-sab\`i wa mā aqlaln, wa Rabbash-shayāṭīni wa mā aḍlaln, wa Rabbar-riyāḥi wa mā dharayn. As'aluka khayra hādhihi ‘l-qaryah, wa khayra ahlihā, wa khayra māfīhā, wa a\`ūdhu bika min sharrihā, wa sharri ahlihā, wa sharri mā fīhā.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and all they overshadow, Lord of the seven worlds and all they uphold, Lord of the devils and all they lead astray, Lord of the winds and all they scatter. I ask You for the goodness of this town, and for the goodness of its people, and for the goodness it contains. I seek refuge in You from its evil, from the evil of its people, and from the evil it contains.
other_duas.reference: Al-Hakim who graded it authentic and Ath-Tfaahabi agreed 2/100, and Ibn As-Sunni (no. 524). Al-Hafidh graded it good in his checking of Al-'Athkdr 5/154. Ibn Baz said in Tuhfatul-'Akhydr p. 37, that An-Nasa'i recorded it with a good chain of narration.
tags: Upon entering a town or village

other_duas.category_name: When entering the market
other_duas.title: When entering the market
other_duas.arabic: لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّه وحدَهُ لا شريكَ لهُ، لهُ المُلْـكُ ولهُ الحَمْـد، يُحْيـي وَيُميـتُ وَهُوَ حَيٌّ لا يَمـوت، بِيَـدِهِ الْخَـيْرُ وَهوَ على كلّ شيءٍ قدير
other_duas.transliteration: Lā ilāha illallāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, Lahu ‘l-mulku wa lahu ‘l-ḥamd, Yuḥyī wa yumīt, wa huwa ḥayyun lā yamūt, Biyadihi ‘l-khayr, wa huwa \`alā kulli shay'in Qadīr.
other_duas.translation: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, Who has no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He brings life and He causes death, and He is living and does not die. In His Hand is all good, and He is Able to do all things.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi 5/291, and Al-Hakim 1/538. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih Ibn Majah 2/21 and Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/152.

other_duas.category_name: When the mounted animal (or mean of transport) stumbles
other_duas.title: When the mounted animal (or mean of transport) stumbles
other_duas.arabic: بِسْـمِ اللهِ
other_duas.transliteration: Bismillāh. With the Name of
other_duas.translation: Allah.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 4/296. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Abu Dawud 3/941.
tags: When the mounted animal (or mean of transport) stumbles

other_duas.category_name: Supplication of the traveller for the resident
other_duas.title: Supplication of the traveller for the resident
other_duas.arabic: أَسْتَـوْدِعُكُـمُ اللَّهَ ال
other_duas.transliteration: Astawdi\`ukumu ‘llāha ‘l-ladhi lā taḍī\`u wadā'i\`uh. I place you in the trust of
other_duas.translation: Allah, whose trust is never misplaced.
other_duas.reference: Ahmad 2/403, Ibn Majah 2/943. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 2/133.
tags: Supplication of the traveller for the resident

other_duas.category_name: Supplication of the resident for the traveller
other_duas.title: Supplication of the resident for the traveller
other_duas.arabic: أَسْتَـوْدِعُ اللَّهَ ديـنَكَ وَأَمانَتَـكَ، وَخَـواتيـمَ عَمَـلِك
other_duas.transliteration: Astawdi\`ullāha dīnak, wa amānatak, wa khawātīma \`amalik. I leave your religion in the care of
other_duas.translation: Allah, as well as your safety, and the last of your deeds.
other_duas.reference: Ahmad 2/7, At-Tirmidhi 5/499. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/155.
tags: Supplication of the resident for the traveller

other_duas.category_name: Supplication of the resident for the traveller
other_duas.title: Supplication of the resident for the traveller
other_duas.arabic: زَوَّدَكَ اللَّهُ التقْوى، وَغَفَـرَذَنْـبَكَ، وَيَسَّـرَ لَكَ الخَـيْرَ حَيْـثُما كُنْـت
other_duas.transliteration: Zawwadaka ‘llāhut-taqwā, wa ghafara dhanbak, wa yassara laka ‘l-khayra ḥaythu mā kunt.
other_duas.translation: May Allah give you piety as your provision, forgive your sins, and make goodness easy for you wherever you are.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi. See Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi, 3/155.
tags: Supplication of the resident for the traveller

other_duas.category_name: Takbir and Tasbih during travel
other_duas.title: Takbir and Tasbih during travel
other_duas.arabic: قَالَ جَابِرٌ رضي الله عنه
other_duas.transliteration: \-- Jabir (ra), said: Whenever we went up a hill we would say Allāhu Akbar (Allah is the Most Great) and when we descended we would say Subḥānallāh (
other_duas.translation: Glory is to Allah).
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 6/135.

other_duas.category_name: Stopping or lodging somewhere in travel and otherwise
other_duas.title: Stopping or lodging somewhere in travel and otherwise
other_duas.arabic: أَعـوذُ بِكَلِـماتِ اللّهِ التّـامّاتِ مِنْ شَـرِّ ما خَلَـق
other_duas.transliteration: A\`ūdhu bikalimāti ‘llāhit-tāmmāti min sharri mā khalaq.
other_duas.translation: I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 4/2080.
tags: Stopping or lodging somewhere in travel and otherwise

other_duas.category_name: While returning from travel
other_duas.title: While returning from travel
other_duas.arabic: يُكَبِّرُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَرَفٍ ثَلاَثَ تَكْبِيرَاتٍ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ
other_duas.transliteration: From every elevated point say Allāhu Akbar (three times), and then recite: Lā ilāha illallāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahu ‘l-mulku, walahu ‘l-ḥamd, wa Huwa \`alā kulli shay'in Qadīr, ā'ibūna, tā'ibūna,\`ābidūn, li Rabbinā ḥāmidūn, sadaqallāhu wa\`dah, wa nasara \`abdah, wa hazama ‘l-'aḥzāba waḥdah. From every elevated point say Allāhu Akbar (Allah is the Most Great) three times and then recite:
other_duas.translation: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, Who has no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is Able to do all things. We return repentant to our Lord, worshipping our Lord, and praising our Lord. He fulfilled His Promise, He aided His slave, and He alone defeated the Confederates.
other_duas.reference: Bukhari 7/163, Muslim 2/980. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say this when returning from a campaign or from Hajj.

other_duas.category_name: What to say upon receiving pleasing or displeasing news
other_duas.title: What to say upon receiving pleasing or displeasing news
other_duas.arabic: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا أَتَاهُ الْأَمْرُ يَسُرُّهُ قَالَ
other_duas.transliteration: When something happened that pleased him, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: Alḥamdu lillāhi ‘lladhi bi ni\`matihi tatimmuṣ-ṣāliḥāt. And if something happened that displeased him, he used to say: Alḥamdu lillāhi \`alā kulli ḥāl. When something happened that pleased him, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say:
other_duas.translation: Praise is to Allah Who by His blessings all good things are perfected. And if something happened that displeased him, he used to say: Praise is to Allah in all circumstances.
other_duas.reference: Ibn As-Sunni, 'Amalul-Yawm wal-Laylah, and Al-Hakim who graded it authentic 1/499. See also Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 4/201.
tags: What to say upon receiving pleasing or displeasing news

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting
other_duas.title: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting
other_duas.arabic: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.translation: \-- The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You shall not enter Paradise until you believe, and you have not believed until you love one another. Shall I tell you of something you can do to make you love one another? Spread the greetings of Salam (peace) amongst yourselves (i.e. between each other).
other_duas.reference: Muslim 1/74 and others.
tags: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting
other_duas.title: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting
other_duas.arabic: ثَلاَثٌ مَنْ جَمَعَهُنَّ فَقَدْ جَمَعَ الْإِيمَانَ
other_duas.translation: Three characteristics, whoever combines them, has completed his faith: to be just, to spread greetings to all people and to spend (charitably) out of the little you have.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 1/82 as a statement of the Companion 'Ammar (RA).
tags: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting
other_duas.title: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting
other_duas.arabic: وَعَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عُمَرَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا
other_duas.translation: \-- \`Abdullah bin \`Umar (RA) said: A man asked the Prophet (ﷺ), "What is the best act of Islam?" He said, "To feed others and to give greetings of Salam (peace) to those whom you know and to those whom you do not know. "
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 1/55, Muslim 1/65.
tags: Excellence of spreading the Islamic greeting

other_duas.category_name: Returning a greeting to a disbeliever
other_duas.title: Returning a greeting to a disbeliever
other_duas.arabic: إذَا سَلَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ فَقُولُوا
other_duas.transliteration: If one of the People of the Scripture (i.e. Christians and Jews) greets you, saying As-Salāmu \`alaykum, then say (to him): Wa \`alaykum. If one of the People of the Scripture (i.e. Christians and Jews) greets you saying As-Salaamu \`alaykum, then say (to him): And upon you .
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/42, Muslim 4/1705.
tags: Returning a greeting to a disbeliever

other_duas.category_name: Upon hearing a rooster crow or the braying of a donkey
other_duas.title: Upon hearing a rooster crow or the braying of a donkey
other_duas.arabic: إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ صِيَاحَ الدِّيَكَةِ فَاسْأَلُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ؛ فَإِنَّهَا رَأَتْ مَلَكاً وَإِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ نَهِيقَ الْحِمَارِ فَتَعَوَّذُوا بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيطَانِ؛ فَإِنَّهُ رَأَى شَيْطَاناً
other_duas.transliteration: \-- When you hear the cock's crow, ask
other_duas.translation: Allah for His favor upon you for surely it has seen an angel. When you hear the bray of a donkey, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, for surely it has seen a devil.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 6/350, Muslim 4/2092.
tags: Upon hearing a rooster crow or the braying of a donkey

other_duas.category_name: Upon hearing the barking of dogs at night
other_duas.title: Upon hearing the barking of dogs at night
other_duas.arabic: إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ نُبَاحَ الْكِلاَبِ وَنَهِيقَ الْحَمِيرِ بِاللَّيْلِ فَتَعَوَّذُوا بِاللَّهِ مِنْهُنَّ؛ فَإِنَّهُنَّ يَرَيْنَ مَا لاَ تَرَوْنَ
other_duas.transliteration: When you hear a dog barking or a donkey braying in the night, then seek refuge in
other_duas.translation: Allah from them, for surely they have seen what you see not.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 4/327, Ahmad 3/306. Al-Albani graded it authentic in Sahih Abu Dawud 3/961.
tags: Upon hearing the barking of dogs at night

other_duas.category_name: For one you have insulted
other_duas.title: For one you have insulted
other_duas.arabic: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma fa'ayyumā mu'minin sababtuhu faj\`al dhālika lahu qurbatan ilayka yawma ‘l-qiyāmah.
other_duas.translation: O Allah, whomever of the believers I have abused, give him the reward of a sacrificial slaughter for it on the Day of Resurrection.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/171, Muslim 4/2007. The wording in Muslim's report is: 'make it a purification for him and a source of mercy.

other_duas.category_name: The etiquette of praising a fellow Muslim
other_duas.title: The etiquette of praising a fellow Muslim
other_duas.arabic: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.transliteration: If any of you praises his companion then let him say: Aḥsibu fulānan wallāhu ḥasībuh wa lā uzakkī \`alallāhi aḥada. If any of you praises his companion then let him say: I consider (such and such a person), and
other_duas.translation: Allah is his Assessor, (meaning: and I cannot claim anyone to be pious before Allah) if you know of this (good character trait in the person) to be such and such (saying what he thinks is praiseworthy in that person).
other_duas.reference: Muslim 4/2296.
tags: The etiquette of praising a fellow Muslim

other_duas.category_name: For the one that have been praised
other_duas.title: For the one that have been praised
other_duas.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ لاَ تُؤَاخِذْنِي بِمَا يَقُولُونَ وَاغْفِرْ لِي مَا لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhumma lā tu'ākhidhnī bimā yaqūlūn, waghfir lī mā lā ya\`lamūn \[waj\`alnī khayran mimmā yaẓunnūn\].
other_duas.translation: O Allah, do not call me to account for what they say and forgive me for what they have no knowledge of \[and make me better than they imagine\].
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, Al-'Adabul-Mufrad no. 761. See Al-Albani, Sahih Al-'Adabul-Mufrad (no. 585). The portion between brackets if from Al-Bayhaqi, Shu'ab Al-Iman 4/228, and comes another account.
tags: For the one that have been praised

other_duas.category_name: The Talbiya for the one doing Hajj or 'Umrah
other_duas.title: The Talbiya for the one doing Hajj or 'Umrah
other_duas.arabic: لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لاَ شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ والنِّعْمَة لَكَ والمُلْكُ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
other_duas.transliteration: Labbayk-Allāhumma labbayk, labbayka lā sharīka laka labbayk, inna ‘l-ḥamda, wanni\`mata, laka wa ‘l-mulk, lā sharīka lak. I am here at Your service,
other_duas.translation: O Allah, I am here at Your service. I am here at Your service, You have no partner, I am here at Your service. Surely the praise, and blessings are Yours, and the dominion. You have no partner.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 3/408, Muslim 2/841.
tags: The Talbiya for the one doing Hajj or 'Umrah

other_duas.category_name: The Takbîr passing the black stone
other_duas.title: The Takbîr passing the black stone
other_duas.arabic: طَافَ النَّبيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم بِالْبَيْتِ عَلَى بَعِيرٍ كُلَّمَا أَتَى الرُّكْنَ أَشَارَ إِلَيْهِ بِشَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ وَكَبَّرَ
other_duas.transliteration: \-- The Prophet (ﷺ) performed Tawaf riding a camel. Every time he passed the corner (containing the Black Stone), he would point to it with something that he was holding and say: Allāhu Akbar (
other_duas.translation: Allah is the Most Great)!
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 3/476. See also 472. The 'something' that was referred to in this Hadith was a cane.
tags: The Takbîr passing the black stone

other_duas.category_name: Between the Yemeni corner and the black stone
other_duas.title: Between the Yemeni corner and the black stone
other_duas.arabic: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا في الدُّنْيَا حسَنَةً وفي الآخِرَةِ حسَنةً وقِنَا عذَابَ النَّارِ
other_duas.transliteration: Rabbanā ātinā fid-dunyā ḥasanah wa fi ‘l-ākhirati ḥasanah wa qinā \`adhāban-nār. Our Lord, grant us the good things in this world, and the good things in the next life, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud 2/179, Ahmad 3/411, Al-Baghawi, Sharhus-Sunnah 7/128. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih Abu Dawud 1/354. The Ayat is from Surat Al-Baqarah, 2:201. ﴿
tags: Between the Yemeni corner and the black stone

other_duas.category_name: When at Mount Safa and Mount Marwah
other_duas.title: When at Mount Safa and Mount Marwah
other_duas.arabic: لَمَّا دَنَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ الصَّفَا قَرَأَ
other_duas.transliteration: Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) approached Mount Safa, he would recite: Innaṣ-Ṣafā wa ‘l-Marwata min sha\`ā'irillāh. Abda'u bimā bada'allāhu bih. He began (his Sa\`y) at Mount Safa climbing it, until he could see the House. He then faced the Qiblah repeating the words: Lā ilāha illallāh, Allāhu Akbar Then he said: Lā ilāha 'illallāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, Lahu ‘l-mulku wa lahu ‘l-ḥamd wa Huwa \`alā kulli shay'in Qadīr, lā 'ilāha illallāhu waḥdahu, anjaza wa\`dahu, wa naṣara \`abdahu, wa hazama ‘l 'aḥzāba waḥdah. Then he would ask Allah for what he liked, repeating the same three times. He did at Mount Marwah as he did at Mount Safa. Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) approached Mount Safa, he would recite: Surely Safa and Marwah are among the signs of Allah. I begin by that which Allah began. He began (his Sa'y) at Mount Safa climbing it until he could see the House. He then faced the Qiblah repeating the words:
other_duas.translation: There is none worthy of worship but Allah, and Allah is the Most Great. Then he said: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, Who has no partner, His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is Able to do all things. None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, He fulfilled His Promise, He aided His slave, and He alone defeated Confederates. Then he would ask Allah for what he liked, repeating the same thing like this three times. He did at Mount Marwah as he did at Mount Safa.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/888. (
tags: When at Mount Safa and Mount Marwah

other_duas.category_name: The Day of 'Arafah
other_duas.title: The Day of 'Arafah
other_duas.arabic: خير الدعاء دعاء يوم عرفة ، وخيرُ ما قلت أنا والنبيُّون من قبلي
other_duas.transliteration: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: The best invocation is that of the Day of Arafat, and the best that anyone can say is what I and the Prophets before me have said: Lā 'ilāha 'illallāhu waḥdahu lā sharīka lahu, lahul-mulku wa lahul-ḥamdu wa huwa \`alā kulli shay'in qadīr.
other_duas.translation: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah Alone, Who has no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is Able to do all things.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi. Al-Albani graded it good in Sahih At-Tirmidhi 3/184, and also Silsilatul-'Ahadith As-Sahihah 4/6.

other_duas.category_name: Remembrance at Muzdalifa
other_duas.title: Remembrance at Muzdalifa
other_duas.arabic: رَكِبَ صلى الله عليه وسلم الْقَصْوَاءَ حَتَّى أَتَى الْمَشْعَرَ الْحَرَامَ فَاسْتَقْبَلَ الْقِبْلَةَ
other_duas.transliteration: 'He (ﷺ) rode Al-Qaswa until he reached Al-MashAAar Al-Haram, he then faced the qiblah, supplicated to
other_duas.translation: Allah, and extoled His greatness and oneness. He stood until the sun shone but left before it rose.'
other_duas.reference: Muslim 2/891.

other_duas.category_name: Takbir when throwing each pebble at the Jamarat
other_duas.title: Takbir when throwing each pebble at the Jamarat
other_duas.arabic: يُكَبِّرُ كُلَّمَا رَمَى بِحَصَاةٍ عِنْدَ الْجِمَارِ الثَّلاَثِ، ثُمَّ يَتَقَدَّمُ، ويَقِفُ يَدْعُو مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبلَةِ، رَافِعاً يَدَيْهِ بَعْدَ الْجَمْرَةِ الْأُولَى وَالثَّانِيَةِ
other_duas.transliteration: \-- The Prophet (ﷺ) said Allāhu Akbar (
other_duas.translation: Allah is the Most Great) with each pebble he threw at the three pillars. Then he went forward, stood facing the Qiblah, and raised his hands and called upon Allah. That was after (stoning) the first and second pillars. As for the third, he stoned it and called out Allāhu Akbar with every pebble he threw, but when he was finished he left without standing at it (for supplications).
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 3/581, 3, 4, and Muslim
tags: Takbir when throwing each pebble at the Jamarat

other_duas.category_name: At times of amazement and that which delights
other_duas.title: At times of amazement and that which delights
other_duas.arabic: سُـبْحانَ الله
other_duas.transliteration: Subḥānallāh! (
other_duas.translation: Glory is to Allah).
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 1/210, 390, 414 and Muslim 4/1857.
tags: At times of amazement and that which delights

other_duas.category_name: At times of amazement and that which delights
other_duas.title: At times of amazement and that which delights
other_duas.arabic: اللهُ أَكْـبَر
other_duas.transliteration: Allāhu Akbar! (
other_duas.translation: Allah is the Most Great)
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 8/441. See also Al-Albani, Sahih At-Tirmidhi 2/103, 235, Ahmad 5/218.
tags: At times of amazement and that which delights

other_duas.category_name: Upon receiving pleasant news
other_duas.title: Upon receiving pleasant news
other_duas.arabic: كَانَ النَّبيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا أَتَاهُ أَمْرٌ يَسُرُّهُ أَوْ يُسَرُّ بِهِ خَرَّ سَاجِداً شُكْراً لِلَّهِ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى
other_duas.transliteration: The Prophet (ﷺ), upon receiving news which pleased him or which caused pleasure, would prostrate in gratitude to
other_duas.translation: Allah blessed and exalted.
other_duas.reference: Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, At-Tirmidhi. See also Al-Albani, Sahih Ibn Majah 1/233, and 'Irwa'ul-Ghalil 2/226.

other_duas.category_name: When feeling some pain in the body
other_duas.title: When feeling some pain in the body
other_duas.arabic: ضَعْ يَدَكَ عَلَى الَّذِي تَألَّمَ مِنْ جَسَدِكَ وَقُلْ
other_duas.transliteration: Put your hand on the place where you feel pain and say: Bismillāh (three times). Then say seven times: A\`ūdhu billāhi wa qudratihi min sharri mā ajidu wa uḥādhir. Put your hand on the place where you feel pain and say: With the Name of Allah (three times). Then say seven times:
other_duas.translation: I seek refuge in Allah and in His Power from the evil of what I find and of what I guard against.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 4/1728.
tags: When feeling some pain in the body

other_duas.category_name: When startled
other_duas.title: When startled
other_duas.arabic: لا إلهَ إلاّ اللّهُ
other_duas.transliteration: Lā ilāha illallāh!
other_duas.translation: There is none worthy of worship but Allah!
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 6/181, Muslim 4/2208.

other_duas.category_name: When slaughtering or offering a sacrifice
other_duas.title: When slaughtering or offering a sacrifice
other_duas.arabic: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
other_duas.transliteration: Bismillāh wallāhu Akbar \[Allāhumma minka wa lak\] Allāhumma taqabbal minnī. With the Name of Allah, Allah is the Most Great! \[
other_duas.translation: O Allah, from You and to You.\] O Allah, accept it from me.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 3/ 1557, Al-Bayhaqi 9/287.
tags: When slaughtering or offering a sacrifice

other_duas.category_name: To ward off the plot of the rebellious devils
other_duas.title: To ward off the plot of the rebellious devils
other_duas.arabic: أَعُوذُ بكَلِمَاتِ اللهِ التَّامَّاتِ الَّتِي لَا يُجَاوِزُهُنَّ بَرٌّ ولَا فَاجرٌ مِنْ شّرِّ مَا خَلقَ، وبَرَأَ وذَرَأَ، ومِنْ شَرِّ مَا يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ وِمنْ شَرِّ مَا يَعْرُجُ فيهَا، ومِن شَرِّ مَا ذَرَأَ في الأَرْضِ ومِنْ شَرِّ مَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا، وِمنْ شَرِّ فِتَنِ اللَّيْلِ والنَّهارِ، ومِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ طارِقٍ إِلَّا طَارِقاً يَطْرُقُ بخَيْرٍ يَا رَحْمَنُ
other_duas.transliteration: A\`ūdhu bikalimāti ‘llāhit-tāmmāti ‘llatī lā yujāwizuhunna barrun wa lā fājirun min sharri mā khalaq, wa bara'a wa dhara', wa min sharri mā yanzilu minas-samā', wa min sharri mā ya\`ruju fīhā, wa min sharri mā dhara'a fi ‘l-arḍ, wa min sharri ma yakhruju minhā, wa min sharri fitani ‘llayli wannahār, wa min sharri kulli ṭāriqin illā ṭāriqan yaṭruqu bikhayr yā Rahmān.
other_duas.translation: I seek refuge in the Perfect Words of Allah -which neither the upright nor the corrupt may overcome - from the evil of what He created, of what He made, and of what He scattered, from the evil of what descends from the heavens, and of what rises up to them, from the evil of what He scattered in the earth, and of what emerges from it, from the evil trials of night and day, and from the evil of every night visitor, except the night visitor who comes with good. O Merciful One.
other_duas.reference: Ahmad 3/419, with an authentic chain of narration, and Ibn As-Sunni (no. 637). Al-Arna'ut, graded its chain authentic in his checking of Al-'Aqidah At-Tahawiyyah p. 133. See also Majma'uz-Zawa'id, 10/127.
tags: To ward off the plot of the rebellious devils

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: قَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.transliteration: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Whoever says: Subḥānallāhi wa biḥamdihi. one hundred times a day, will have his sins forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Whoever says:
other_duas.translation: Glorified is Allah and praised is He. one hundred times a day, will have his sins forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 7/168, Muslim 4/2071, see also invocation no. 91 of this book.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.transliteration: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Whoever says: Lā ilāha illallāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, lahu ‘l-mulku wa lahu ‘l-ḥamd wa huwa \`alā kulli shay'in Qadīr. ten times, will have the reward for freeing four slaves from the Children of Isma'il. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Whoever says:
other_duas.translation: None has the right to be worshipped but Allah alone, Who has no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He is Able to do all things. ten times, will have the reward for freeing four slaves from the Children of Isma'il.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 7/67, Muslim 4/2071, see also invocation no. 93 of this book.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.transliteration: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Two words are light on the tongue, weigh heavily in the balance, and are loved by the Most Merciful One: Subḥānallāhi wa biḥamdih, Subḥānallāhi ‘l-\`Aẓīm. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: Two words are light on the tongue, weigh heavily in the balance, and are loved by the Most Merciful One:
other_duas.translation: Glorified is Allah and praised is He, Glorified is Allah the Most Great.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari 7/168, Muslim 4/2072.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.transliteration: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: For me to say: Subḥānallāh, walḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illallāh, wallāhu 'Akbar is dearer to me than all that the sun rises upon (i.e. the whole world). Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: For me to say:
other_duas.translation: Glory is to Allah, and praise is to Allah, and there is none worthy of worship but Allah, and Allah is the Most Great. is dearer to me than all that the sun rises upon (i.e. the whole world).
other_duas.reference: Muslim 4/2072.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.translation: \-- Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "Is anyone of you incapable of earning one thousand Hasanah (rewards) in a day?" Someone from his gathering asked, "How can anyone of us earn a thousand Hasanah?" He said, "Glorify Allah a hundred times and a thousand Hasanah will be written for you, or a thousand sins will be wiped away."
other_duas.reference: Muslim 4/2073.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: مَنْ قَالَ
other_duas.transliteration: Whoever says: Subḥānallāhi ‘l-'Aẓīmi wa biḥamdih will have a date palm planted for him in Paradise. Whoever says:
other_duas.translation: Glorified is Allah the Most Great and praised is He. will have a date palm planted for him in Paradise.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi 5/511, and Al-Hakim who graded it authentic and Ath-Thahabi agreed 1/501. See also Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 5/531 and Sahih At-Tirmidhi3/160.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.transliteration: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "O Abdullah bin Qais, should I not point you to one of the treasures of Paradise?" I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." So he told me to say: Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata 'illā billāh. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: "O Abdullah bin Qais, should I not point you to one of the treasures of Paradise?" I said, "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." So he told me to say: There is no power and no might except by Allah.
other_duas.reference: Al-Bukhari, cf. Al-Asqalani, Fathul-Bari 11/213, Muslim 4/2076.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: وَقَالَ صلى الله عليه وسلم
other_duas.transliteration: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: The most beloved words to Allah are four: Subḥānallāh Walḥamdu lillāh. Wa lā ilāha illallāh Wallāhu Akbar. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said: The most beloved words to Allah are four: Glorified is Allah, and The praise is for Allah, and
other_duas.translation: There is none worthy of worship but Allah, and Allah is the Most Great.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 3/1685.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: جَاءَ أَعْرَابِيٌّ إِلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ
other_duas.transliteration: A desert Arab came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "Teach me a word that I can say. " The Prophet told him to say: Lā ilāha illallāh waḥdahu lā sharīka lah, Allāhu Akbaru kabīra, walḥamdu lillāhi kathīra, Subḥānallāhi Rabbil-\`ālamīn, Lā ḥawla wa lā quwwata illā billāhi ‘l-\`Azīzil-Hakīm. He said, "That is for my Lord, but what about me?" The Prophet (ﷺ) told him to say: Allāhummaghfir lī, warḥamnī, waḥdinī warzuqnī. A desert Arab came to Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and said, "Teach me a word that I can say. " The Prophet told him to say: There is none worthy of worship but Allah, Who has no partner, Allah is the Great, the Most Great, and praise is to Allah in abundance, glory is to Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no power and no might but by Allah the Mighty, the Wise. He said, "That is for my Lord, but what about me?" The Prophet (ﷺ) told him to say:
other_duas.translation: O Allah forgive me, and have mercy on me and guide me, and provide for me.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 4/2072, Abu Dawud reports the same Hadith with the addition: and when the Arab left, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "He has filled his hands with goodness." 1/220.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: كَانَ الرَّجُلُ إِذَا أَسْلَمَ عَلَّمَهُ النَّبيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الصَّلاَةَ ثُمَّ أَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَدْعُوَ بِهَؤُلاَءِ الْكَلِمَاتِ
other_duas.transliteration: Whenever anyone accepted Islam, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach him how to pray then he would instruct him to invoke Allah with the following words: Allāhummaghfir lī, warḥamnī, waḥdinī, wa \`āfinī warzuqnī. Whenever anyone accepted Islam, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach him how to pray then he would instruct him to invoke Allah with the following words:
other_duas.translation: O Allah forgive me, and have mercy on me and guide me and give me good health and provide for me.
other_duas.reference: Muslim 4/2073, and in one of Muslim's reports there is the addition: 'For these words combine \[the goodness of\] this world and the next.'
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir

other_duas.category_name: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.title: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
other_duas.arabic: إِنَّ أَفْضَلَ الدُّعَاءِ
other_duas.transliteration: The most excellent invocation is: Alḥamdulillāh and the most excellent words of remembrance are: Lā ilāha illallāh. The most excellent invocation is:
other_duas.translation: Praise is for Allah. and the most excellent words of remembrance are: There is none worthy of worship but Allah.
other_duas.reference: At-Tirmidhi 5/462, Ibn Majah 2/1249, and Al-Hakim who graded it authentic and Ath-Tbahabi agreed 1/503. See Al-Albani, Sahihul-Jami' As-Saghir 1/362.
tags: Excellence of Tasbih, Tahmid, Tahlil, and Takbir
